$comment: Time-boxed exceptions to the blocking high/critical npm-audit gate.
An entry here is a DEBT RECORD, not a dismissal. Every field is load-bearing,
and since H60 (2026-08-18) check-audit.mjs ENFORCES that — a missing field is
a MALFORMED failure, because an entry with no `revisitAfter` compares
`undefined < today` === false and so never expires: it switches its own
time-box off, which is the one property that stops this file decaying into a
suppression list.
advisory      the GHSA id, so the entry is greppable against the report
package       the vulnerable package (NOT the transitive parents)
workspace     which lockfile it lives in
severity      as reported by npm audit
why           why it is not fixable TODAY — must name what was tried
reachability  the honest exploitability call, with the evidence for it
revisitAfter  ISO date. PAST THIS DATE THE BUILD FAILS. Not a snooze —
it forces the assessment to be re-made, not inherited.
removeWhen    the concrete condition that retires this entry
owner         which surface owns the decision — an exception nobody owns
is nobody's to revisit
mitigation    the compensating control that exists TODAY. An exception with
no stated mitigation is a dismissal in a justification's
clothes.
check-audit.mjs also fails on a STALE entry (listed but no longer reported),
so a fixed advisory cannot quietly keep its exception — and it matches on the
ADVISORY, never the package name, so an entry cannot silently absorb a NEW
advisory that lands on the same package.

why: ADDED 2026-11-17. picomatch ReDoS through single-branch repeated extglobs; vulnerable <=4.0.7.
Installed: 4.0.7, through tinyglobby/fdir under electron-builder 26.18.0's chain
(@electron/rebuild, node-gyp and app-builder-lib are reported as its transitive parents).
THERE IS NO PATCHED RELEASE TO TAKE. Measured from the registry today: 4.0.7 is the
newest picomatch, so neither a bump nor an override can reach a fixed version. npm's
suggested fix is electron-builder 24.13.3, a MAJOR DOWNGRADE of the packager (26 → 24),
which would trade a build-time ReDoS for two years of packager fixes. Not taken.
reachability: NOT REACHABLE FROM ANY SHIPPED ARTIFACT OR UNTRUSTED INPUT. A ReDoS needs an attacker to
supply the glob PATTERN. picomatch runs only inside electron-builder while it packages the
app, matching patterns from our own committed build config against our own files.
Evidence (2026-11-17, main ba48f05c9): clients/desktop has NO `dependencies` (package.json),
and `build.files` is ["src/**/*","setup/**/*","branding.json"], so electron-builder packs
none of node_modules into the app. Every flagged package is `dev: true` in
clients/desktop/package-lock.json. No file under clients/desktop/src or setup imports it,
and no .github workflow builds the desktop app: electron-builder runs only through
`npm run build:mac|linux|win` on a maintainer's machine.
The worst case is a slow local build on a maintainer's machine.
exceptions.removeWhen: picomatch publishes a release above 4.0.7 that fixes GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf (then bump or override it, and delete this entry), or electron-builder's chain stops depending on a vulnerable picomatch.
exceptions.mitigation: The packaged app contains none of this tooling (no runtime dependencies; build.files excludes node_modules). Packaging runs only on maintainer machines, against repo-controlled patterns. check-audit keeps desktop's devDependencies in scope, so a fixed release turns this entry STALE and forces its removal.

why: ADDED 2026-11-17. minimatch DoS via globparts amplification; vulnerable >=7.0.0 <11.0.1.
reports it under app-builder-lib's high, beside GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf.
A fixed minimatch exists (11.0.1+), but @electron/universal requires ^9. Forcing 11 with an
override puts an untested MAJOR under the macOS universal-binary step. Proving that safe
needs a real packaging run (an Electron download and a signed build), which is a bigger
risk to the release than a build-time DoS. Not taken today.
reachability: NOT REACHABLE FROM ANY SHIPPED ARTIFACT OR UNTRUSTED INPUT. The amplification needs an
attacker-supplied glob. @electron/universal uses minimatch only while merging the macOS
x64 and arm64 builds, on patterns from electron-builder's own config.
Evidence (2026-11-17, main ba48f05c9): clients/desktop has NO `dependencies` (package.json),
and `build.files` is ["src/**/*","setup/**/*","branding.json"], so electron-builder packs
none of node_modules into the app. Every flagged package is `dev: true` in
clients/desktop/package-lock.json. No file under clients/desktop/src or setup imports it,
and no .github workflow builds the desktop app: electron-builder runs only through
`npm run build:mac|linux|win` on a maintainer's machine.
The worst case is a slow local macOS build.
exceptions.removeWhen: @electron/universal (via electron-builder) moves to minimatch >=11.0.1, or a packaging run proves an override to minimatch 11 safe for build:mac. Then delete this entry.
exceptions.mitigation: As for GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf: no runtime dependencies, so node_modules is not packaged; packaging runs only on maintainer machines, against repo-controlled patterns; and the entry goes STALE (and must be deleted) once the advisory stops being reported.
